formats.key: Permit(address holder,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 expiry,bool allowed)
effects: When allowed is true, the holder's Polygon DAI allowance for the spender is set to the maximum uint256 (unlimited), replacing any earlier allowance.
When allowed is false, the holder's Polygon DAI allowance for the spender is set to 0, which revokes any earlier allowance.
Once the permit is submitted, the spender can move all of the holder's DAI with transferFrom, pull or move. The allowance has no end date.
Anyone can submit the signature until expiry. If expiry is 0, they can submit it at any time. Submitting it uses up the holder's current nonce.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender as a raw address, "Unlimited spending: true/false" as a raw boolean, and "Valid until" as a date, which disappears when expiry is 0.

findings.title: Permit: allowed=false revokes the allowance, but the screen still says 'Authorize spending' with 'Unlimited spending: false'.
findings.evidence: UChildDAI.sol permit(): `uint wad = allowed ? uint(-1) : 0; _approve(holder, spender, wad);`. Descriptor: intent "Authorize spending of tokens", field `allowed` label 'Unlimited spending' format raw. With false, a signer reads this as a limited authorization, but the code sets the allowance to 0.
findings.fix: Map `allowed` through an enum (true → 'Unlimited DAI allowance', false → 'Revoke allowance (set to 0)'), and make the intent neutral, e.g. 'Set DAI allowance'.

findings.title: Permit: the intent names neither DAI, the spender, nor that the approval is unlimited.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Authorize spending of tokens", interpolatedIntent absent. Case 0 shows only 'Unlimited spending: true'. The amount actually approved is uint(-1) DAI (UChildDAI.sol permit()).
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Allow {spender} to spend unlimited DAI' and label the field 'DAI allowance'.

findings.title: Permit: the spender is shown as a raw address instead of addressName.
findings.fix: Use format addressName with types ["contract","eoa"] and sources ["local","ens"].

findings.title: Permit: 'Valid until' suggests the approval ends then; it only limits when the signature can be submitted.
findings.evidence: UChildDAI.sol permit(): `require(expiry == 0 || now <= expiry, ...)` checks only at submission. The allowance set by _approve never expires. Descriptor label 'Valid until' on `expiry`.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Signature deadline' or 'Submit before', and add a note that the allowance itself does not expire.

findings.title: Permit: expiry=0 means the signature never expires, but the field is hidden in that case.
findings.evidence: Descriptor `expiry` visible {ifNotIn:[0,"0"]}. Code: `expiry == 0 || now <= expiry`, so 0 means the signature can be submitted at any time. The screen shows no deadline and does not say it never expires.
findings.fix: Keep the field visible and render 0 as 'No deadline (never expires)'. If no such format exists, at least do not hide it.

findings.title: Permit: the domain name 'Dai Stablecoin' likely differs from the contract's name '(PoS) Dai Stablecoin'.
findings.evidence: UChildDAI.sol initialize(): `_initializeEIP712(name_, ERC712_VERSION)`. The domain name is the token name stored at initialization. Descriptor metadata.owner and case 0 screen.owner are '(PoS) Dai Stablecoin', while context.eip712.domain.name is 'Dai Stablecoin'. Real permits would not match the descriptor, and messages that do match produce signatures the contract rejects.
findings.fix: Set domain.name to the on-chain name() value ('(PoS) Dai Stablecoin'), after confirming it on chain.

findings.title: Permit test case 0 uses a domain with chainId, but UChildDAI signs with salt instead.
findings.evidence: UChildDAI.sol EIP712Base: `EIP712Domain(string name,string version,address verifyingContract,bytes32 salt)` with salt = bytes32(chainId). cases/0.json domain {name, version, chainId:137, verifyingContract}. A signature over that message is invalid on this contract.
findings.fix: Rewrite the test message with the domain the contract uses: name, version, verifyingContract, salt = 0x…89.

findings.title: Permit: the contract's domain has no chainId field, only salt, so wallets cannot bind by chainId.
findings.evidence: UChildDAI.sol EIP712Base: domain typehash uses `bytes32 salt` = chainId, with no chainId field. Descriptor deployments bind on chainId 137 plus the address.
findings.fix: No descriptor change. Note that wallets must resolve chain binding from salt or verifyingContract.

Permit(address holder,address spender,ui.worst: Permit: expiry=0 means the signature never expires, but the field is hidden in that case.

summary.worst: Permit: expiry=0 means the signature never expires, but the field is hidden in that case.
